elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section e makes “all results of the Support Services” and other materials prepared specifically for Client the sole property of Client.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The broad references to “all results” and “any other materials prepared by TrueLink specifically for Client” cover work product created for Client.

elements.element: Vendor presently assigns all right, title and interest in those deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: TrueLink “hereby assigns to Client all right, title and interest therein.”

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of all of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly preserves TrueLink’s ownership only in the Interface and treats embedded TrueLink IP as licensed rather than assigned. It contains no general reservation covering all pre-existing TrueLink intellectual property.

elements.element: If Vendor intellectual property is embedded in deliverables, Vendor grants Customer a license to that embedded intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The condition is expressly addressed: “To the extent any TrueLink Intellectual Property is embedded in such results or materials, TrueLink grants Client” a license to it.

elements.element: The license to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP license is expressly “perpetual.”

elements.element: The license to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP license is expressly “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The license to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP license is expressly “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Client retains all right, title and interest in Client Content and all data provided by or on behalf of Client or its customers, brokers or borrowers. The existing Section 8(d) license does not transfer ownership.

elements.element: No jointly owned intellectual property is created.
elements.evidence: The clause states: “No jointly owned intellectual property is created under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: Neither the Interface ownership sentence nor the embedded-IP license expressly reserves ownership of all generic tools, including tools developed or used in performing the services.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic know-how.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no express ownership reservation for TrueLink’s generic know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a license covering the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Client receives the broader right of ownership in the deliverables, together with a license to any embedded TrueLink IP as part of those deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are perpetual.
elements.evidence: The ownership assignment has no expiration, and the embedded-IP license is expressly perpetual.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The present ownership assignment contains no revocation right, and the embedded-IP license is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are worldwide.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP license does not state that it is worldwide. The worldwide language in Section 8(d) applies to TrueLink’s Credit Data license, not Client’s deliverable rights.

elements.element: Customer's rights in the deliverables are royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP license is expressly royalty-free, and no continuing royalty is imposed on Client’s ownership of the deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may use the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Ownership permits Client to use the deliverables, and the embedded-IP license permits the TrueLink IP to be used as part of them.

elements.element: Customer may modify the deliverables.
elements.evidence: Although ownership permits modification of Client-owned portions, the embedded TrueLink IP license does not expressly permit modification, so modification of the complete deliverables is not assured.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The embedded TrueLink IP license contains no sublicensing right, so Client cannot clearly sublicense all rights needed for deliverables containing that IP.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its deliverable rights for its business.
elements.evidence: Client’s ownership and embedded-IP license are not restricted to nonbusiness purposes and therefore cover use in Client’s business.

result.reason: The redline substantially achieves the customer-ownership position, including a present assignment, Customer Data ownership, the required embedded-IP license attributes, and no joint ownership. It does not expressly reserve all pre-existing Vendor IP, only the Interface and implicitly embedded TrueLink IP. The fallback also fails because generic tools and know-how are not reserved and the embedded-IP license lacks worldwide, modification, and sublicensing rights. No complete level is reached, so the redline is not minimal under the stated definition. Existing Interface ownership, the Credit Data license, and unrelated term provisions remain operative without a clear contradiction.
